  • MX17 detector basics: dead strips, gain maps, drift gaps, saturation, X footprint 2026-10-19Cosmic benchMicromegasDetector model

    det4’s amplitude-dependent X width was its dead strips; strip-scale gain maps and strip health for five chambers; drift gaps 28.1–31.5 mm measured without timing; saturation handled per event; the RC model’s X χ² deficit is its footprint width. Plus the drift-velocity consistency, saturation and asymmetry follow-ups.

  • det3 X neighbour asymmetry: real, in the raw ADC, and det3’s own 2026-10-19DetectorCrosstalk

    From the rawest observable up: det3’s June-15 build copies ~0.1–0.2 of each X pulse into the next channel, only when the charge sits over a Y pad, at every Y pad; det4/det7 the same at a third. Its size follows the cluster width (gas, drift field). Not gas flow, not the resistive stripes; the parity split is partly peak selection; det3 fits a one-sided X reach on the bus side, ~20× the copper value.
